assessment.nobel_worthiness: A fundamental statistical-mechanical account of two-dimensional melting that established a durable conceptual framework for topological defects and phases.
assessment.attribution: The listed theorists are central to the defect-mediated theory and its decisive renormalization-group development.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested across decades in varied two-dimensional systems and have become standard physics.
uncertainties: The extent to which experimental realizations show the full idealized transition sequence can depend on system details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Exact fluctuation relations transformed nonequilibrium statistical mechanics by identifying universal constraints far from equilibrium.
assessment.attribution: Evans initiated seminal fluctuation results, while Jarzynski and Crooks supplied distinct exact work-relation formulations of exceptional breadth.
assessment.maturity: The relations are rigorously understood and extensively tested computationally and experimentally.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of recognition among the closely related formulations requires careful historical assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory supplied an unusually effective and conceptually clear route into strong electronic correlations.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt and collaborators developed the infinite-dimensional foundation, and Georges and Kotliar were pivotal in the modern formulation and impact.
assessment.maturity: It is a mature, widely used theoretical framework with extensive contact to correlated-material experiments.
uncertainties: Its importance is partly methodological, and the foundational credit extends beyond any simple three-person account.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-dimensional conformal field theory revealed exact structure at criticality and has reshaped statistical and quantum field theory.
assessment.attribution: The named contributors made foundational, complementary advances in conformal symmetry and critical phenomena.
assessment.maturity: Its consequences have been assimilated for decades across statistical physics, strings, and quantum matter.
uncertainties: The attribution boundary between this body of work and broader conformal-field-theory developments is inherently wide.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks unite beautiful quantum control with an extraordinary advance in precision measurement and fundamental tests.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept, while Ye made defining experimental advances and applications.
assessment.maturity: Their performance, reproducibility, and scientific uses are now firmly demonstrated.
uncertainties: The field has several major experimental contributors, so the boundary of individual credit needs scrutiny.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic band gaps established a powerful physical analogy between electronic and electromagnetic waves and enabled a major field.
assessment.attribution: John and Yablonovitch supplied seminal independent concepts, with Joannopoulos central to theoretical development and realization.
assessment.maturity: The field has matured through broad experimental confirmation and technological influence.
uncertainties: Applications have been diverse rather than concentrated in a single defining device.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phase and the Aharonov-Bohm effect exposed profound, experimentally consequential aspects of quantum phase and gauge structure.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov is inseparable from the effect and Berry from the general adiabatic geometric phase.
assessment.maturity: Both concepts are exceptionally mature and experimentally established across quantum systems.
uncertainties: They are distinct discoveries, so their suitability as a single prize formulation requires judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices created a remarkably clean experimental laboratory for many-body quantum physics and simulation.
assessment.attribution: The listed experimental leaders made landmark realizations, though theoretical and experimental credit is unusually broad.
assessment.maturity: The platform is mature, versatile, and has generated sustained advances in quantum many-body science.
uncertainties: Five credited names exceed the Nobel limit and make a fair attribution difficult.
